value.rationale: The natural p² residue-ring lift of the cubic graph is the first nonreduced model in the finite Fourier restriction setting. The result supplies a complete, not merely averaged, ordered two-sum law uniformly over every p≥5, separates four genuinely different positive multiplicity levels from singular p-adic valuation strata, determines sumset size and gives the exact constant-input fourth Fourier moment. This provides an explicit structural benchmark for extension and additive-energy questions over residue rings beyond the field case; it is not just an arbitrary numerical sample or a repackaged general theorem. It does not claim an unrestricted sharp extension inequality.
